reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2, E3) from the same paper directly demonstrates each key premise: synthesis of disordered HEA nanoparticles by 55 ms Joule heating, a 5 min reheat at ~1100 K to induce ordering, prevention of growth/agglomeration by limited heating time, and trapping by ~10^4 K/s cooling, all for an octonary noble-metal system. The premises are accurately represented and fully supported.
premises: Rapid Joule heating of metal salt precursors at ~1100 K for tens of ms yields disordered solid-solution HEA nanoparticles
A secondary reheat at ~1100 K for ~5 min promotes a disorder-to-order transition to a single-phase MPEI structure
The short reheat duration prevents particle coarsening and phase separation
Rapid cooling (~10^4 K/s) kinetically traps the ordered structure
The process works for compositions with >5 noble metals where precursors decompose near 1100 K
